name: 20359-shortchat-qwen25-32b-pp4
hardware: 4x H100 80GB HBM3 -- four GPUs of one a3 node (`--gres=gpu:4`), one node.
parallelism: PP=4, TP=1, DP=1, `mp` executor, one in-process engine driven by guidellm's `vllm_python` backend. 64 layers split 16/16/16/16. Four stages are fixed; a different depth is a different setup.
architecture: Qwen2ForCausalLM dense: 64 layers, hidden 5120, 40 query / 8 key-value heads, head_dim 128, 32768 positions; ~32.8B parameters, ~65 GB in bf16.
load_profile: poisson (OPEN loop), 25 req/s, 10% warmup and 10% cooldown by request count, bounded at 2048 requests with a 1200 s safety cap. The rate is the one number that may move, and 25 is the hardware translation of the source's 16: the author's 4x A100 setup retired 8.88 req/s against 16 offered -- 1.80x oversubscribed -- and that oversubscription is what the TTFT tail is made of. Scaling that ceiling by the H100/A100 dense-bf16 ratio 494.7/312 = 1.586 gives 8.88 x 1.586 = 14.1 req/s here, so 1.80x needs 14.1 x 1.80 = 25.4 -> 25 req/s (1.78x). At the declared 16 this hardware would be only 1.13x oversubscribed. Confirm rather than assume: the run's `request throughput` must come back below 25.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, 225 prompt and 157 output tokens, fixed (min = max = mean), no prefix buckets -- ~382 tokens per request, ~59% prompt and ~41% generation. The backend renders the prompt through the checkpoint's chat template, so the engine counts a couple of dozen tokens more than 225, and sets ignore_eos with max_tokens so every generation runs its full 157.
purpose: A short-turn chat assistant on a 32B model, serving 25 requests per second across four GPUs.
launch:
# vLLM 0.9.1-era engine args: an unknown key is an error at engine construction, not a warning.
model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct

# 64 layers / 4 = 16 per stage, an exactly even split, so VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION is not needed.
pipeline-parallel-size: 4
tensor-parallel-size: 1

distributed-executor-backend: mp
enable-chunked-prefill: true
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# The source's resident set, restored. Little's law on the author's own PRE block -- 8.88 req/s x
# 73.05 s mean E2EL -- puts ~649 requests resident. Left unset, this engine takes 128: guidellm
# calls `from_engine_args` with no `usage_context`, so `_set_default_args_v1`'s device tables are
# skipped and `SchedulerConfig.__post_init__` supplies 128. That is a harness artifact, not a
# choice of the source, and the resident set is what BOTH halves of the mechanism act on -- the
# decode budget is `num_decode_tokens / pp_size`, and the `len(running) == max_num_running_reqs`
# break is what forms the TTFT tail. 640 is 649 rounded to an exact multiple of pp_size.
# It also keeps POST on the right side of the roofline: the crossover batch where a stage stops
# being weight-bound is (16.25 GB / 3.35 TB/s) / (2 x 8.125e9 / 143.5 TFLOP/s) = 4.85 ms /
# 0.113 ms = 43 tokens. POST microbatches are 640/4 = 160, well past it -- as the author's
# 649/4 = 162 were past the A100's equivalent 44. At the default 128 they would be 32, i.e. below
# it, and the split would pay less than it did for the author.
max-num-seqs: 640
